hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-01.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-01.body:
The square in row $r$, column $c$ carries the number $8(r-1)+c$, which is odd iff $c$ is odd. Square $1$ (row $1$, column $1$) is black, so a square is black iff $r+c$ is even. A black square with odd number therefore has $c$ odd and $r$ odd: $4$ choices of row times $4$ choices of column $=16$.

**Answer: 16**

hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-02.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-02.body:
The worst case is pulling out all the blue, green and khaki socks first: $20+30+40=90$ socks, none red. So $90$ socks do not suffice. Conversely, any set of $91$ socks must contain every colour: a set missing a colour has at most $90$ socks (the largest total of three colours is $20+30+40=90$). So $91$.

**Answer: 91**

hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-03.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-03.body:
The inner expression equals the whole expression, so $3=\sqrt{x+3}$. Squaring: $9=x+3$, so $x=6$. (For $x=6$ the nested radical converges to $3$, since the limit $L$ of $\sqrt{6+L}$ satisfies $L^2-L-6=0$, $L=3$.)

**Answer: 6**

hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-04.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-04.body:
Initially the bead hangs $13$ inches below the joined hands (half the string). After the bead rises $8$ inches it is $5$ inches below the hands, with $13$ inches of string to each hand. By Pythagoras, each hand is $\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12$ inches horizontally from the bead, so the hands are $24$ inches apart.

**Answer: 24 inches**

hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-09.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-gen2-09.body:
Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. Then $OM\perp AB$, $MB=12$, $OB=15$, so $OM=9$. Since $C$ is on ray $AB$ beyond $B$, $MC=12+28=40$, and $OC=\sqrt{9^2+40^2}=41$.

**Answer: 41**
